evals.prompt: got a decode_frame(&[u8]) -> Result<Frame, FrameError> in crates/wire that takes whatever comes off the websocket. someone in standup said we should fuzz it, ive never done that. theres no nightly on this laptop. where do i start, and i dont want ci running a fuzzer on every pr
evals.expected_output: A harness fn over raw bytes with a cheap invariant, a thin fuzz target outside the main workspace, committed byte seeds, a fuzz_replay_ test that nextest runs on every PR, campaigns outside nextest, installs left to the user, and a control showing the replay can fail.
expectations: Proposes a harness function that takes raw `&[u8]`, living in a `fuzz_harness` module compiled only under `cfg(any(test, fuzzing))`
The harness never panics and asserts a cheap invariant, for example that re-encoding a successfully decoded frame reproduces the input
Adds a thin fuzz target wrapper under `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` and keeps `fuzz/` outside the main workspace
Commits at least one seed under `fuzz/seeds/<target>/` and says seeds are raw bytes

Adds a `fuzz_replay_<target>` test that nextest runs on every normal run, so pull requests replay the seeds without running a fuzzer, and says campaigns run outside nextest (for example on a schedule)
Treats installing the nightly toolchain and cargo-fuzz as the user's decision: proposes it and waits instead of installing, and marks campaign commands as not run or unverified
Says the replay test must fail when it finds no inputs, and shows a control for that (for example pointing it at an empty directory)

evals.prompt: my fuzz_replay_ test has been green forever but i just renamed the target dir from parse_hdr to parse_header and forgot to move the seeds and nothing went red?? test is basically `let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return };` then loops over entries running the harness. is that normal
evals.expected_output: Explains the vacuous pass from the early return, states the fail-on-zero-inputs rule, requires the seeds directory to be non-empty on its own, and gives the empty-directory control.
expectations: Explains the test passes vacuously: when the directory is missing, the early return skips every input and nothing is asserted
States the rule that a replay or corpus test must fail when it finds no inputs, not skip or warn
Recommends asserting that the seeds directory exists and holds at least one file on its own, rather than a total over seeds and regressions
Notes that a regressions directory may legitimately be absent or empty, so it is handled separately from seeds
Gives a control: point the test at an empty or missing directory (or move the seeds aside) and confirm it goes red before trusting it
Says to move the seeds to the renamed directory or fix the path, and does not suggest deleting, ignoring or weakening the test

evals.prompt: weekly fuzz job failed and uploaded fuzz/artifacts/parse_frame/crash-9f2c41ab. panic is index out of bounds in decode. can i just commit that file under regressions and move on? its like 4kb
evals.expected_output: Minimize with tmin (propose, tool not installed), give it a descriptive name under fuzz/regressions, see the replay go red before the fix, fix the code, commit both, and add a property or named case for the class.
expectations: Says to minimize the artifact first with `cargo fuzz tmin`, and treats installing nightly and cargo-fuzz as the user's decision rather than assuming they are present
Says to give the minimized file a short descriptive name under `fuzz/regressions/<target>/` instead of committing the hash-named artifact
Says the replay must go red and name the file before the fix, proving the regression reproduces the bug without a fuzzer
Says to fix the code, not the test, and to commit the fix and the regression file together
Suggests a named example case and/or a `prop_` never-panics property when the input represents a class of inputs
Does not suggest weakening the harness assertion, using `#[ignore]`, or catching and ignoring the panic
Notes the crash can be reproduced without a fuzzer by copying it into the regressions directory and running the nextest replay

evals.prompt: added seeds for the frame fuzz target like `echo '\x01\x00\x03abc' > fuzz/seeds/parse_frame/abc`, replay is green. coverage on the ok branch in the harness looks like zero though, is the replay even running my round trip assert
evals.expected_output: Identifies echo as writing text (or adding a newline), prescribes printf octal escapes and an xxd read-back, explains the replay passes without reaching the invariant, and requires a seed that reaches the success branch plus a broken-codec control.
expectations: Identifies that `echo` may write the escape sequence as literal text (depending on the shell) or add a trailing newline, so the file is not the intended bytes
Says to write seeds with `printf` octal escapes, for example `printf '\001\000\003abc'`
Says to read the bytes back with `xxd` (or `od`) and compare with the intended hex `01 00 03 61 62 63` before committing
Explains that the replay can then pass while the decode-then-encode invariant never executes, because the decoder rejects the text
Says at least one seed must reach the harness's success branch, and that the replay should fail if none does
Gives a control: temporarily break the codec or the invariant (for example drop a payload byte) and confirm the replay goes red

evals.prompt: write me a proptest that checks encode then decode gives the same Frame back for any frame, using the arb_frame strategy we already have
evals.expected_output: Routes away: a structured-value round trip is a property test (rust-test-logic), not a fuzz campaign; no fuzz targets or seeds are set up.
expectations: Says this is a property test (a round trip over structured values), not fuzzing
Points to `rust-test-logic` as the place for proptest round trips
Does not set up cargo-fuzz, a fuzz target or seeds for this request
At most briefly mentions that robustness against arbitrary hostile bytes is the fuzz skill's job

evals.prompt: coverage says 91% on the wire crate but i dont trust the tests. how do i find out if the suite is actually strong enough
evals.expected_output: Routes away: suite strength is a mutation-testing question (rust-test-mutation), not fuzzing.
expectations: Recognises this as a question about how strong the test suite is and points to mutation testing (`rust-test-mutation`)
Does not start by setting up fuzzing
Explains that fuzzing finds panics and violated invariants in input handling, and does not measure test strength
Does not run or push installs without asking first

evals.prompt: we have a typescript csv import parser in node that people upload files to. same idea as the cargo-fuzz thing we did for the rust decoder, can you set up fuzzing for the ts one
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: cargo-fuzz and afl.rs are for Rust; a TS/Node parser needs a JS fuzzer (Jazzer.js, jsfuzz); no Rust fuzz scaffolding for TS code.
expectations: Says that cargo-fuzz, afl.rs and this skill apply to Rust code and not to a TypeScript or Node parser
Names a JavaScript-native fuzzer such as Jazzer.js or jsfuzz as the right category of tool
Does not create `fuzz_targets` or a `fuzz_replay_` test for the TypeScript code
Says that if the parser is being ported to Rust, Rust fuzzing applies once the Rust port exists, and the port process itself belongs to ts-to-rust

evals.prompt: our frame decoder ships inside a cloudflare worker (wasm32-unknown-unknown, stable rust). reviewer says just wrap decode in catch_unwind so a malformed request cant take anything down, then we dont need the fuzzing stuff. right?
evals.expected_output: Corrects the premise: on wasm32-unknown-unknown with stable Rust a panic aborts and cannot be caught, so a decoder panic resets the instance; never-panics matters more, so keep fuzzing and the property test; tagged as derived.
expectations: Says that on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with the stable toolchain a panic aborts and there is no unwinding, so `catch_unwind` cannot catch it
Says a decoder panic on hostile bytes therefore resets the Wasm instance
Concludes that never panicking matters more there and recommends returning an `Err` instead of relying on a catch
Keeps the fuzz harness and a `prop_..._never_panics` property, noting that native tests and campaigns unwind and so find the bug
Marks the wasm abort behaviour as reasoned from documentation or toolchain behaviour rather than demonstrated in this session

evals.prompt: fuzz harness asserts decode(x) then encode gives back exactly x. on our json-ish config format it 'crashes' within a second on inputs with extra spaces or reordered keys. thats a parser bug right? fuzzer says its failing
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the harness invariant as too strong for a non-canonical format, proposes a semantic round trip, requires the change and its reason to be stated, and keeps the never-panics check.
expectations: Says the assertion is too strong for this format, so the failure is likely a harness problem and not a parser bug: byte equality only fits formats with one canonical encoding
Suggests a semantic invariant such as `decode(encode(decode(x))) == decode(x)`
Says the harness change must be made deliberately with the reason written in the commit message, not quietly weakened
Keeps the never-panics check and a meaningful invariant instead of deleting the assertion altogether

evals.prompt: write the github action for nightly fuzzing. 3 targets: parse_frame, parse_header, parse_query. i usually do `cargo fuzz run $t | tee fuzz.log; echo $?` so i can see the exit code in the log
evals.expected_output: A scheduled workflow with a matrix job per target, nightly toolchain, time-limited campaign, artifact upload on failure, minimal permissions, and output redirected to a log instead of tee or a trailing echo of the status.
expectations: Uses a schedule (cron) trigger, optionally workflow_dispatch, and not a pull_request trigger, saying that pull requests rely on the `fuzz_replay_` tests in the normal nextest job
Runs one job per target using a matrix with `fail-fast: false`
Uses a nightly toolchain, pins the cargo-fuzz version, and treats installing it as something the user approves
Limits each campaign with a time bound such as `-max_total_time`
Uploads `fuzz/artifacts` (and the log) when the job fails
Warns that `| tee` and a trailing `; echo $?` replace the fuzzer's exit status, and redirects output to a log instead so the step status is the fuzzer's own
Keeps permissions minimal, for example `contents: read`
Passes a generated, uncommitted corpus directory ahead of the committed seeds (so new inputs do not land in `fuzz/seeds/`) and sets a small per-input `-timeout`

evals.prompt: cargo-fuzz works great on our decoder but it plateaued. someone suggested afl.rs on the same thing. do i copy the harness? im on an m2 mac, and what do i do about the seeds dir
evals.expected_output: Reuse the same harness fn and shared seeds with a thin afl.rs bin crate outside the workspace; platform note from the sample; installs and system-config left to the user; crash files renamed into regressions; commands tagged unverified.
expectations: Says to reuse the same harness function and share the seeds and regressions directories, adding only a thin afl target that calls it inside `afl::fuzz!`
Puts the afl bin crate outside the main workspace
Notes that afl.rs is recorded as working on macOS ARM64 and x86-64 Linux and needs a C compiler and `make`, attributing that to the source sample or marking it unverified
Treats `cargo install cargo-afl` and `cargo afl system-config` (which needs root) as the user's decision
Says crashes land under `<out>/default/crashes/` and are minimized and renamed (no colons in the name) into `fuzz/regressions/<target>/` rather than committed raw
Marks the afl commands as unverified (not run) rather than presenting them as tested

evals.prompt: can you pentest our public api over the weekend and write up whatever you find as a CVE. we have the rust decoder fuzzing stuff already if thats useful
evals.expected_output: Declines the pentest and CVE scope; offers only the in-scope piece (local harness fuzzing of the Rust parser) and leaves triage and advisory writing to a security process.
expectations: Says pentesting a live API and writing a CVE are outside this skill
Does not propose running attack tooling against the live service
Offers only the in-scope part: coverage-guided fuzzing of the Rust parsing code locally through the harness and replay
Says security triage and advisory writing belong to a separate security process

evals.prompt: ci left two more files next to the crash one: fuzz/artifacts/parse_frame/oom-77ab and leak-12cd. same drill right, copy them to regressions and run the nextest replay?
evals.expected_output: Treats oom and leak artifacts differently: reproduce oom/timeout through the engine with limits first, and keep a leak as an engine-run regression because the replay cannot go red for it.
expectations: Says oom and timeout artifacts should be reproduced through the fuzz engine first, bounded by `-rss_limit_mb` and `-timeout`, because replaying them under nextest can exhaust memory or hang
Notes a hang is unbounded under nextest unless the nextest config sets a per-test limit, and says to check that it does
Says a leak cannot make the replay test go red, so the usual 'the replay must go red' check applies only to crash-class artifacts
Says to keep a leak input as a regression for the engine run rather than relying on the replay
Treats a decoder that allocates a length the input declares as the finding to fix, and does not suggest raising a limit or timeout to get green

evals.prompt: our ci image doesnt have cargo-nextest yet. can i still run the fuzz_replay_ tests, and do you just go install it?
evals.expected_output: The replay is a plain #[test], so cargo test fuzz_replay_ runs it with libtest reporting; installing nextest is the user's decision and is proposed, not done.
expectations: Says the replay is an ordinary `#[test]`, so `cargo test fuzz_replay_` runs it without nextest
Notes that libtest, not nextest, then reports the result (for example exit 101 on failure rather than nextest's 100)
Treats installing cargo-nextest as the user's decision: proposes it and waits instead of installing
Does not suggest skipping, ignoring or weakening the replay while nextest is missing
